label: Madhubani
summary: Bihar folk art: bold double outlines, hatching, fish and sun motifs
history: Painted for centuries by women of Mithila on walls and floors for weddings and festivals; later on paper and cloth. Recognised with a GI tag.
look: Bold double outlines, every shape packed with fine hatching, no empty space; fish, sun, peacock and lotus motifs in natural pigment colours.

line.quality: Steady, deliberate; inner line parallel to the outer

fill: Fine parallel hatching, cross-hatching and dots inside every shape

characters.proportions: Stylised, large almond eyes in profile, long noses
characters.faces: Profile view with one large fish-shaped eye
characters.poses: Formal, frontal or profile; ceremonial gestures
characters.costume: Patterned saris and dhotis filled with hatching

environment.sky: Not drawn — paper filled with motifs
environment.ground: Not drawn — figures float in patterned space

border: Double-line border filled with repeating geometric or floral pattern, drawn on progressively

composition.framing: Full frame bordered on all four sides

motion.feel: Lines drawing on, gentle swimming and swaying
